newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish shares end flat, Nordbanken jumps.
newsitem.headline: Swedish shares end flat, Nordbanken jumps.

text.p: Sweden's bourse ended flat on Wednesday, pulled one way by a strong rise in the banking sector but dragged the other by a tumbling forestry sector and temporary weakness in Ericsson.
The general index closed unchanged at 2,016.23 after a fairly active day's trade when shares worth 4.3 billion crowns changed owners.

A focus of the day was Nordbanken whose trading was suspended early morning. The bank later announced a proposed five billion crown share buy back and its share price jumped. It closed 13.50 crowns higher at 149 crowns.
The bank sector soared 4.22 percent in Nordbanken's wake. Handelsbanken rose five crowns to 135, S-E-Banken climbed 1.50 to 58.50 crowns and Swedbank was three up at 86.50 crowns.
The forestry sector, however, suffered a day of losses, tumbling 2.48 percent amid market speculation that North American and Scandinavian stocks rose in August.
MoDo fell 6.50 crowns to 186.50 crowns and Stora lost 3.50 to 90 crowns.
Telecoms giant Ericsson had a volatile day, losing up to 4.50 crowns after rival Motorola painted a bleak outlook for the third quarter of the year.
But by the close it recovered some ground and ended 1.50 crowns lower at 159 crowns.
Drugs major Astra was 2.5 crowns lower at 278 crowns.
Brokers said the market had underlying strength.
"If it goes well in the U.S. we will see a strong day tomorrow," one broker said.
